_comment: granite5_ctc / granite-speech-5.0-470m-turboctc-nc tolerances. Stage 4 FINALIZED.
Per-variant file, NOT tests/tolerances/granite5_ctc.json (finalized for the Apache-2.0
sibling). Same architecture and same C++ code, different weights; they drift very
differently and must not share a budget. The golden manifest points here.
Correctness regime (every number below measured in exactly this one):
GGUF:      granite-speech-5.0-470m-turboctc-nc-BF16.gguf, the reference tier - BF16
weights, F32 norms/biases/BN stats, F16 conv kernels.
KV cache:  none. encoder-ctc is one forward pass; --kv-type reaches no graph.
Frontend:  the production C++ path (MelFrontend per_utterance + host deltas +
2-frame stacking). No reference-mel injection. `mel.in` is a real
frontend-parity gate, not a pinned read, and it passes at the Stage 2
magnitude budget with no widening (observed 1.8e-05 vs budget 1.5e-04).
Backend:   CPU, --threads 1 (scripts/validate.py defaults).
Reference: transformers 5.17.0 GraniteSpeech5ForCTC at F32, eager attention,
torch-threads 1.
Cases:     jfk (1100 mel frames, even) and dots (3533, odd); each entry is the max
over both.
Coverage: ALL 16 encoder blocks are dumped and gated here (34 distinct tensors), not
the 6-block default the Apache sibling used. The extra blocks were added during Stage 4
because they are what localized the mechanism below. They are cheap; they stay.
Recipe: finalized = max(1.5 x observed_cpp_drift, magnitude_budget, 1e-6), with
magnitude_budget the Stage 2 rule (1e-4 x p99_abs for max, 1e-5 x rms for mean).
Baseline: ggml's BF16 matmul rounds the F32 activation to BF16 before the dot product,
so the C++ computes BF16 x BF16 against an F32 x F32 reference. The BF16 and F32 GGUFs
built from this checkpoint hold numerically identical weights, so this is arithmetic,
not weight rounding.
Amplifier: a MASSIVE-ACTIVATION CHANNEL. Encoder blocks 10-13 carry one outlier channel
(570 on this checkpoint) at |value| 190-481 while the rest of the same tensor sits at
20-28. That single channel carries 34-73% of all squared error in those tensors. It is
created inside block 10 (block 9's peak is 28.7) and is squashed again by the final
LayerNorm, surviving in enc.out as a single-frame spike: on dots the worst frame is 1 of
441 at 0.219, with the next-worst at 0.044.
The Apache sibling has the same kind of channel (612) at a SIMILAR magnitude, yet drifts
10-35x less at blocks 10-13. Magnitude does NOT explain the gap - apache block 12 has a
LARGER peak (248.8 vs 229.9) and 23x LESS drift. The difference is how conditioned each
checkpoint's accumulation is on that channel, which is a property of the weights.
=== WHY THIS IS ARITHMETIC AND NOT A BUG (evidence, not assertion) ===========
0. BF16 REFERENCE CONTROL (the strongest check; added after CJ asked whether any of
this points at our own inference being wrong). The reference was re-run at
--dtype bf16 so torch-BF16-vs-torch-F32 can be compared against ours-vs-torch-F32
on identical tensors. OUR BF16 IS CLOSER TO THE F32 REFERENCE THAN PYTORCH'S OWN
BF16 IS, at every gated tensor, on BOTH checkpoints (ratio 0.3-0.6x):
tensor             torch BF16    ours      torch BF16   ours     (nc | apache)
We are not amplifying BF16 error; we absorb less of it than the reference does.
This also independently confirms the nc-vs-apache asymmetry that magnitude could
not explain: torch itself puts nc at 9.1x / 11.2x / 9.6x / 12.5x the apache drift
at blocks 11/12/13 and enc.out (we see 35.5x / 23.2x / 33.1x / 10.0x - same
direction and order). The asymmetry is a property of the -nc checkpoint under BF16
arithmetic, reproduced by a second implementation, not something our code creates.
Our nc/apache SPREAD is wider than torch's at blocks 11-13 only because we are
unusually accurate on apache there (7-9x better than torch) while 1.6-2.9x better
on nc; in absolute terms we are below torch's error in every cell.
Scope: CPU thread-1 regime, dots. Does not cover Metal or the quantized tiers.
1. F32 CONTROL. The same C++ graph on an F32 GGUF of the SAME checkpoint, same CPU
thread-1 regime, drops drift by 100-2500x against the same F32 reference:
A graph, masking, indexing or shape bug does not disappear when the storage dtype
changes. This is the decisive check; it rules out the code.
2. Blocks 0-9 drift within 0.66-1.10x of the Apache sibling - identical behavior. Only
the outlier-channel blocks diverge.
3. CTC output depends only on the per-frame argmax over 16384 logits. Argmax agreement
with the reference is 441/441 on dots and 137/137 on jfk.
4. Safety margin (reference top-2 logit gap minus twice that frame's logit drift) is
positive on every frame of both cases. Minimum 0.804 logits at a frame whose drift
is 0.024 - a 34x margin. Tight-gap frames and high-drift frames are disjoint: the
largest-drift frame (14 on dots, drift 0.731) sits on a 4.97-logit gap.
5. Full LibriSpeech test-clean: C++ BF16 batch 1 = 1.29% WER vs the Stage 2 Oracle
reference 1.29% (gate <= REF + 0.01pp). Error composition 519/82/82 against the
reference's 519/83/82.
6. Only 2 of 2620 hypotheses differ from the reference at all, and on one the C++ is
the better transcription.
7. Batch 8 is byte-identical to batch 1 across all 2620 hypotheses.
The factors below are large, and larger than the Apache sibling needed. Read them with
care: the denominator is 1e-4 x p99_abs, and p99_abs describes the 99% of elements that
are SMALL while the error lives on the one channel that is not. Against the element's
own magnitude the same drift is 1.7-4.0%. The p99-relative view is the misleading one
for a tensor with a 50x outlier channel; it is kept only because the tolerance framework
compares absolute values.
Production variants - quantized GGUFs, GPU backends - drift differently. Those
measurements belong in Stage 6/7 reports, NOT in this file.
Entries above the Stage 2 magnitude budget: 33 of 34.
Largest widening factors (tensor, factor vs magnitude budget, observed max drift):

enc.out                     1909.0x   observed 2.187e-01  (p99_abs 1.718)

enc.ctc_logits               637.2x   observed 7.307e-01  (p99_abs 17.2)

mel.in
STAGE 5 WATCH ITEM: the channel-570 outlier (|value| up to 481, ~20x the rest of
its tensor) is exactly what K-quant block scales handle worst, since it dominates
the scale of whatever block it lands in. Treat Q4_K_M / Q5_K_M WER on this variant
as a real risk rather than a formality; the Apache sibling's quant results do not
transfer.
